title: OverlayFS snapshotter inode bloat -> eviction delays (post-incident notes)
content:
Summary:

- On 2024-09-20 02:13 UTC we observed a progressive increase in pod startup latency across eu-west-1 GPU nodes. P95 pod start time rose from ~3s baseline to ~28s; cluster autoscaler reported backlog of pending pods awaiting scheduling. Several tiling-worker jobs experienced OOMKilled during startup and then long Pending windows.

- Root cause (short): overlayfs+containerd snapshotter inode leak (growth in overlayfs lowerdir inode table) caused the host to hit inode exhaustion on the ephemeral root partition on a subset of GPU nodes. Kubelet could not create checkpoints / new container directories -> kubelet & containerd API timeouts -> kube-scheduler saw NodeNotReady/unschedulable flaps and started pacing pod placement. Eviction thresholds were crossed (rootfs.inodesFree < configured threshold) causing aggressive pod eviction waves.

Detection and signals:
- Alert: node-inline-metrics:node-rootfs-inodes-low fired for ~8 nodes at 02:10 UTC.
- Grafana dashboards: host_root_inodes_free dropped from ~1.2M to <5k over ~45 minutes on affected nodes.
- Containerd logs showed repeated errors: "snapshotter: failed to prepare snapshot: no space left on device" and later "overlay: inode table full, overlayfs failed to create new inode".
- Kubelet logs: repeated 504s when contacting container runtime; errors around creating pod sandbox and writing checkpoint files.
- Symptoms: many pods stuck in ContainerCreating with mount/unpack timeouts; some already-running pods served traffic intermittently as overlayfs responded slowly.

Timeline (abridged):
- 01:40 UTC: batch job churn increases (scheduled tryouts for model build), spike in pod churn on GPU fleet.
- 02:05 UTC: first node alerts for inode low. Ops channel noisy, paging for multiple nodes.
- 02:10-02:30 UTC: escalations, manual SSH show rootfs inode usage near 100%; attempted local GC (containerd snapshotter GC) had no effect — GC itself hung due to accessing overlay tables.
- 02:40 UTC: emergency mitigation: cordon + drain on highest-pressure nodes and migrate new workloads to warm reserve pool (dedicated spare nodes).
- 03:00 UTC: identify snapshotter bug; revert recent snapshotter change rolled out three days earlier (PR #56) which changed reference counting during overlay cleanup.
- 03:35 UTC: revert rollout to previous snapshotter; start rolling restart of containerd & kubelet (graceful).
- 04:30 UTC: inode usage begins to drop as previously stuck GC completes on restarted nodes; pod startup p95 trending back to baseline by 06:00 UTC.

Impact:
- ~12 nodes in eu-west-1 impacted; ~280 pods evicted; ~740 pods experienced >30s startup delay; two customer-facing endpoints saw degraded 5xxs for ~90 minutes due to downstream worker unavailability and circuit-breaker trip.
- Cost: increased autoscaler churn (extra nodes spun up), estimated transient compute spend +$4.2k.

Root cause analysis (detailed):
- Regression introduced in snapshotter PR #56 modified the overlay snapshot garbage collection reference counting to be slightly more aggressive in degenerate overlay lowerdir layouts. Under high pod churn with many small containers (our model-build batch jobs), this code path failed to reconcile references for a subset of overlay metadata blobs. Over time the lowerdir inode table entries accumulated (soft-deleted metadata) and were not reclaimed.
- The overlayfs implementation in the kernel expects timely unlink/cleanup patterns; containerd snapshotter GC uses an async reconcile loop which, due to a race, sometimes skipped reclaiming inodes when heavy churn aligned with an intermediate state. The net effect: inode counters on the filesystem increased without releasing the inode quota.
- Once inode exhaustion reached, processes attempting to create directories/files fail even if raw byte space is available. Kubelet relies on creating per-pod directories and checkpoint files — those failing manifest as ContainerCreating hang and kubelet reporting NodeNotReady conditions to the control plane.

Temporary mitigations applied during incident:
- Cordoned and drained the worst affected nodes to stop new pod placements.
- Rotated containerd to previous stable binary via systemd on affected hosts, which allowed GC to run in non-racy code path and freed inodes.
- Increased inode alert sensitivity so we can catch faster during next surge (alert rule lowered from 2% to 5% free).
- Raised ephemeral rootfs inode soft threshold to trigger earlier process-level backpressure instead of full eviction (short term config tweak).

Permanent fixes and follow-ups (action items):
- Engineering: finalize and merge snapshotter PR revert with a proper fix for reference counting race (owner: Priya Shah, JIRA-OPS-3421). Target: 2024-10-05 for merge and canary rollout.
- SRE: add a proactive cron job that scans /proc/*/mounts + df -i across GPU fleet and reports nodes entering inode growth trend (owner: Evan Cho). Complete by 2024-10-01.
- Kubelet ops: change kubelet checkpointing to write to a separate partition (or tmpfs if ephemeral) to avoid eviction avalanche when root inode exhaustion occurs. Evaluate switching /var/lib/kubelet to a partition with larger inode density for GPU nodes. (owner: Lena Morales).
- Observability: add synthetic pod-create tests in eu-west-1 that run during batch windows to surface slow ContainerCreating (p95 > 10s) before customer impact. (owner: eng-sre infra).
- Runbook update: create a dedicated runbook for inode exhaustion on ephemeral rootfs with quick triage steps, including commands below. (owner: Marcel Ortega).

Runbook (draft triage steps) — very terse checklist for oncall:
1) Check alerts: kubernetes.node.rootfs.inodes.low (Grafana/Alertmanager).
2) On impacted node: ssh node -> run: df -i /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/kubelet /
   - expect: if InodesFree < 1k -> high risk.
3) containerd logs: journalctl -u containerd -n 500 | grep snapshotter
   - look for: "failed to prepare snapshot", "inode" messages.
4) kubelet logs: journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 | grep -E "ContainerCreating|checkpoint"
5) Quick mitigation: cordon node (kubectl cordon <node>), then drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data, but if drain is slow prefer to Cordon only and move new traffic to reserve nodes.
6) If GC appears stuck: restart containerd (systemctl restart containerd) on one node at a time to allow GC to run and reclaim inodes. Avoid mass restarts.
7) If restart fails to free inodes: escalate to eng-sre and snapshotter owners; capture strace/containerd stack (see linked artifact PR).

Commands used during triage (examples):
- df -i /var/lib/kubelet /var/lib/containerd /
- sudo find /var/lib/containerd -xdev -type f -printf '%s %p\n' | sort -rn | head -n 40
- journalctl -u containerd -o short-iso | grep -i snapshotter | tail -n 200
- sudo du -sh /var/lib/containerd/* | sort -h

Notes / Lessons learned (informal):
- Inode exhaustion is an underrated failure mode — alerts often focus on bytes free but not inodes. Our worker node images have relatively small inode tables (large mkfs -t defaults with big block size) which makes us susceptible under many small files.
- Recent rollout cadence for snapshotter changes was fast; we should gate snapshotter GC changes behind a longer canary period on a small batch of nodes that host bursty batch jobs.
- Consider reserving a small percentage of nodes with alternate fs layout (higher inode density) as a hot reserve for high-churn workloads.
- Possibly move ephemeral model build workloads to use tmpfs for build artifacts instead of overlay-backed images where practical.

Open questions (to resolve in postmortem):
- Why did local GC hang when run in-situ on some nodes? hypothesis: containerd process inherited file handles to the stale overlay files preventing unlink; need deeper investigation with kernel-level tools (debugfs) — action: schedule kernel-level excavation with infra eng.
- What is the appropriate inode alerting threshold to balance noise vs early detection? propose: test 10k and 5k thresholds over 2 weeks. (owner: Marcel Ortega).

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Node samples (anonymized): node-eu-gpu-12, node-eu-gpu-18, node-eu-gpu-23 (see attached node dump in linked confluence).
- Relevant PRs: snapshotter PR #56 (regression), revert PR #78 (temporary revert), long-term fix PR (in review).
- Jira: JIRA-OPS-3421 (root cause + postmortem).

-- Marcel (notes, WIP).
